assessment.nobel_worthiness: Hardware correction of spherical aberration in electron lenses overcame a limit set by Scherzer's theorem and made routine sub-angstrom imaging and spectroscopy possible in TEM and STEM. It is a clear, specific invention with large downstream effect across materials physics, chemistry and nanoscience, and it fits the 'discovery or invention' criterion well. From my own field I can see directly that the instrument changed what can be measured at interfaces, defects and nanoparticles.
assessment.attribution: Rose supplied the multipole corrector design and theory, Haider led the first working TEM implementation with Urban's group and Uli Dahmen-type collaborations, and Urban's group demonstrated atomic-resolution use in materials. The three credited names form a clean, compact configuration. Other major contributors, such as Krivanek and Dellby for STEM correctors, are not on the supplied credit list and I cannot add them.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed for over two decades by commercial adoption in thousands of instruments and a long record of independent results. The interpretation is stable and recognition would be timely, with no sign of premature judgment. Related awards exist, which I recall only from general knowledge and have not verified here.
uncertainties: The STEM corrector line (Krivanek, Dellby) is outside the credited names, so the allocation may be seen as incomplete.
Whether the prize committee would regard this as physics or as an instrumentation/materials achievement is a judgment call.
Exact attribution of the first working corrector between Haider, Rose and Urban's groups is from memory.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Theory of flat moire bands at the magic angle in twisted bilayer graphene and the experimental discovery of correlated insulators and superconductivity opened a new field of tunable correlated quantum matter. Originality is high and the conceptual clarity is excellent, with a very strong follow-on literature in moire materials.
assessment.attribution: The Bistritzer and MacDonald continuum model predicted the magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero and collaborators found the correlated states and superconductivity. A theory-plus-experiment three-person prize is plausible, though the experimental side involves a larger team, with Cory Dean and others also prominent in moire physics outside the supplied names.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced by many groups with consistent core phenomenology within roughly eight years. The origin of the superconductivity and the full phase diagram are still debated, so the field is young, but the existence of the phenomena is secure.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity remains unsettled.
Sample-dependence and twist-angle disorder complicate the experimental record.
Fair allocation between the experiment team and other moire-materials pioneers is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Z2 topological insulator and the quantum spin Hall effect established a new classification of electronic phases based on topology and spin-orbit coupling, with robust edge and surface states. Very high conceptual importance and wide impact on condensed matter, materials discovery and spintronics.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele provided the theoretical prediction; Molenkamp's group observed the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe quantum wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and the 3D topological insulator experimentalists (Hasan and others), are not in the credited names, so credit is contested and the three-person configuration leaves out significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed in HgTe and later in three-dimensional materials with ARPES and transport. Mature and timely, though the Nobel Committee has already honoured topological phases in 2016, so the incremental claim must be argued carefully.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2016 prize for topological phase transitions.
Credit split between theory proposals (BHZ) and experiment is contested and only partly captured by the credited names.
Practical edge-channel transport is less clean than the ideal picture.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock, using the magic wavelength idea to trap many atoms while cancelling light shifts, brought fractional uncertainty to the 1e-18 level and opened relativistic geodesy and fundamental-constant tests. A clear and specific invention with major impact in precision measurement.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength concept and led the early realisation; Jun Ye's group drove the strontium lattice clock to record accuracy. Other groups (Lemonde, Ludlow, Hinkley and others) contributed, but a two-person award is defensible from the supplied credit.
assessment.maturity: Many independent clocks agree at the 1e-18 level and international comparisons are under way. Mature, and recognition seems timely given an expected redefinition of the second.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 and 2012 prizes in frequency combs and trapped-ion control.
Others, such as the ion-clock community, might claim comparable standing.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and of TXS 0506+056 and NGC 1068 opened neutrino astronomy at TeV-PeV energies. Originality of the instrument concept and its scientific results are both high.
assessment.attribution: Halzen was the central scientific leader of IceCube and Spiering was an early driving figure in the neutrino telescope programme from AMANDA and the Baikal and Lake neighbours. The supplied credit has two names; the collaboration is large and the role of other pioneers (for example the DUMAND initiators) is a possible allocation concern, which the committee would need to examine.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is firmly detected; source identification is still thin, with evidence at a few sigma for individual sources. Reasonably mature for the discovery of the flux, but source astronomy is still developing.
uncertainties: Individual-source evidence is only a few sigma.
Allocation among the collaboration leadership and earlier DUMAND and Baikal pioneers is uncertain.
Prior prize recognition for neutrino astronomy (Davis, Koshiba) may shape how the committee frames it.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED applied cavity-QED ideas to superconducting circuits, giving strong coupling, dispersive readout and the architecture used in most superconducting quantum processors. Clear, original and of lasting importance across quantum information and engineering-driven physics.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf proposed it; Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. Four names are credited, and I would choose three; Girvin is a strong theoretical contributor and the cut is a real allocation problem.
assessment.maturity: Widely replicated and now the backbone of a large industry effort. The science is mature, though the committee has recently recognised superconducting-circuit quantum effects, so timing and overlap need care.
uncertainties: Close overlap with the recent prize on macroscopic quantum effects in circuits.
Excluding Steven M. Girvin is a difficult attribution choice.
Technology development may be seen as engineering rather than a single discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Large room-temperature tunnel magnetoresistance in junctions, followed by coherent tunnelling in MgO barriers, underlies hard-disk read heads and magnetic random access memory. This is physics with huge practical impact, and as a materials physicist working with interfaces I value the importance of interface quality and crystalline barriers here.
assessment.attribution: Miyazaki and Moodera reported room-temperature TMR in 1995; Parkin and Yuasa/Djayaprawira groups realised giant MgO TMR in 2004, with Butler and Mathon providing the theory. The supplied three names omit Yuasa and the theorists, so allocation is unsettled.
assessment.maturity: Fully mature and commercially established for about two decades. The giant magnetoresistance prize of 2007 covers closely related ground, which may make the committee cautious about recognising this next step.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2007 prize for giant magnetoresistance.
Credit for the MgO result is shared with groups not named, and with theorists.
Whether the work counts as discovery or technology development.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The three-step recollision model and its quantum theory explain high-harmonic generation and underpin attosecond science and strong-field imaging. It is conceptually clear and fundamental, and I know its importance directly from the 2023 prize work on attosecond methods.
assessment.attribution: Corkum and Schafer et al. introduced the semiclassical model in 1993, and Lewenstein et al. gave the quantum theory in 1994. A three-person prize looks coherent, though Kulander and others also contributed and the 2023 laureates already received the attosecond-pulse prize.
assessment.maturity: Extremely well confirmed by experiments across atoms, molecules and solids. The theory is stable, but the 2023 prize makes a second recognition in the same area harder to justify as timely.
uncertainties: Strong overlap with the 2023 attosecond prize.
Credit among Kulander, Schafer, Corkum and Lewenstein is intertwined and could be disputed.
Whether the committee sees this as a separate discovery from attosecond pulses.
